newsitem.title: ITALY: CYCLING-CIPOLLINI TREBLE ENDS IN CONTROVERSY.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-CIPOLLINI TREBLE ENDS IN CONTROVERSY.

text.p: A day after losing his Giro d'Italia lead, Mario Cipollini triumphed for the third time in four days on Tuesday. But it was tinged with controversy.
The Italian's team mate Gian Matteo Fagnini was thrown out of the race by officials for what they alleged was "dangerous riding" at the finish of the 156 kms stage from San Marino.

Fagnini set the pace to bring the sprint ace to the front, but as he swung away in the final 200 metres to allow Cipollini to sprint, officials claimed Fagnini came close to forcing two riders into the spectator barriers.
It was Cipollini's 19th Giro victory and he needs one more to rise into the top 10 stage winners in the 80-year history of the Italian tour.

"I still hope for two more victories in this Giro which would beat my personal best of four in 1992. My next chance will be at Mondragone on Friday," said the Tuscan, whose professional career started in Arezzo nine years ago.
Endrio Leoni added a second place on Tuesday to his two third placings in his daily battle with Cipollini, and Spain's Angel Edo was third.
Cipollini's victory earned him a deduction of 12 seconds from his overnight deficit of 2:03 on leader Pavel Tonkov.
The Russian clings to a one-second advantage on his compatriot Yevgeny Berzin as the fifth day takes them 215 kms to the mountain top finish of Terminillo.
During Tuesday's skirmishing over undulating roads, Berzin tried to win the intermediate sprint which gives the first three deductions from their total race times.
He missed out and Tonkov said: "Maybe this is the only way he can take the jersey from me. Perhaps he is afraid of what may happen when we are in the mountains."
After several fruitless attacks Gabriele Colombo's final gamble as the race entered Arezzo ended with a crash.
As the 1996 Milan-San Remo classic winner took a bend his bike slipped away, sending the Italian into a heap in the gutter just before the final kilometre.
It cost him his fifth overall position as he finished more than a minute behind the pack of 169 riders.
